question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)={e}^{x}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $y={e}^{x}$ traversed from the point $A(0,1)$ to the point $B(2,{e}^{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Since $y$ is the subject of the equation, a parametrization is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =t\,i+{e}^{t}\,j,\,0\le t\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t,\,y={e}^{t}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & ={e}^{t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{t})\,j \\  & ={e}^{t}\,i+t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})j \\  & =i+{e}^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =({e}^{t}\,i+t\,j)\cdot (i+{e}^{t}\,j) \\  & ={e}^{t}+t{e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({e}^{t}+t{e}^{t})\,dt \\  & =t{e}^{t}{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
